transcript.system:
You operate the user's GitHub account, project files and MongoDB deployment through the tools provided. Complete the user's task, then stop.

This server fronts several toolboxes, each wrapping another server, and offers two ways to use their tools. For a single action or a short chain where you look something up and then act on it, call search_tools to find a tool in any box, or a box's own search_<box> tool to look inside that box; without a query, a box's search lists the box and leads with its own guidance. Then call describe_tool to see a tool's arguments and call_tool for each step, reading each result before the next. Author an XState v5 state machine and run it with execute_machine only when the work loops or branches over results, takes many steps, or is a workflow worth saving (call discover_apis first for every box's tool types, the authoring contract, and worked examples). Either way, tools that change something may pause and ask the user to approve that specific action before it runs; each tool's listing says whether it runs immediately or asks for approval.

Toolboxes — tools are named <box>.<tool>; search a box with its search_<box> tool, then pass the full name to describe_tool, call_tool and toolCall:
- fs — The user's project files (14 tools)
- github — GitHub: issues, PRs and repos for acme/widgets (95 tools)
- mongo — The shop MongoDB deployment (21 tools)

Use code mode (discover_apis, execute_machine) for this task.

content.content:
Projection code mode over the toolboxes fs, github, mongo.

XState version: 5.32.5 (pinned). Importable modules: 'xstate', '@astral-mcp/tools'. Nothing else resolves; there is no network and no filesystem.

Tools: 130 across the toolboxes fs, github, mongo — too many to list here (fs: 14, github: 95, mongo: 21). Call search_tools (every box) or the search_<box> tool of a box (search_fs, search_github, search_mongo) to find tools by name or purpose and describe_tool for a tool's arguments by its qualified name, <box>.<tool> (types: true adds its TypeScript); the full definitions are in projection://types/tools.d.ts, one tools.<box> property per box.

Projection authoring contract (execute_machine)

Write ONE module whose only top-level statements are imports and a single
default-exported XState v5 machine. The module is re-evaluated on every
approval round trip, so top-level side effects are rejected.

  import { setup } from 'xstate';
  import { toolCall } from '@astral-mcp/tools';

  export default setup({}).createMachine({ /* ... */ });

Rules:
1. Default-export a machine built with XState v5 setup(...).createMachine(...).
   XState v4 Machine(...) is rejected.
2. Machine context must be JSON-serializable at all times. No Map, Set, Date,
   class instances, functions, undefined, bigint or symbols in context.
3. Request tools with the toolCall action. NEVER wrap a tool call in
   fromPromise/invoke — restored snapshots restart invoked actors, which
   would re-execute an approved write. Machines using invoke are rejected.
4. After a toolCall, wait in a state for one of these events:
     TOOL_RESULT { callId, result }   the call succeeded
     TOOL_ERROR  { callId, error }    the call failed
     TOOL_DENIED { callId, reason }   the user declined, or policy denies it
   Denial is not an abort: handle TOOL_DENIED and continue or finish.
   IMPORTANT: if your machine has more than one call outstanding at the same
   time (parallel regions), give each toolCall an explicit id and guard every
   waiting state with whenCall(id) — events reach every region that can
   handle them, so an unguarded region will consume another call's result:

     import { toolCall, whenCall } from '@astral-mcp/tools';
     entry: toolCall('fs.write_file', () => ({ path: '/a' }), { id: 'a' }),
     on: { TOOL_RESULT: { guard: whenCall('a'), target: 'done' } },
5. Tools marked "asks for approval" pause the machine for user approval;
   tools marked "runs immediately" do not. The arguments captured at that
   moment are the arguments that execute.
6. Only 'xstate' and '@astral-mcp/tools' resolve as imports. There is no
   filesystem, no network, no fetch. All working state lives in context.
7. Finish by reaching a final state. Use the machine's output for the result.
8. TOOL_RESULT.result is the tool's structuredContent when the server returns
   one (see its Output type in tools.d.ts); otherwise the text of its single
   text block, null for an empty result, or the raw content array for
   anything else. A tool that returns isError arrives as TOOL_ERROR. Tools
   without an Output type are typed unknown, and that does not mean text:
   many servers return an object without declaring it, and JSON text
   arrives as a string. Never parse a result you have not seen: run the
   read on its own first (call_tool, or a machine whose output is
   event.result) and write the machine against the shape it returns.
9. Tool inputs such as paths, ids and names are server-specific. Do not guess
   them: take them from the machine's input, or discover them first with a
   read-only call (a list/search tool) and keep what you learn in context.
10. Tool names on this server are qualified: <box>.<tool>. Each box's tools
    sit under tools.<box> in tools.d.ts; pass the qualified name to toolCall,
    e.g. toolCall('fs.read_file', ...) (sample names; use the names in tools.d.ts).
    An unqualified name is rejected. One machine may call tools in several
    boxes; every call that asks for approval is approved on its own.

Example — happy path with a read-only call (run with input: { path }):

  import { setup, assign } from 'xstate';
  import { toolCall } from '@astral-mcp/tools';

  export default setup({}).createMachine({
    id: 'readOne',
    context: ({ input }) => ({ path: input.path, result: null }),
    initial: 'reading',
    states: {
      reading: {
        entry: toolCall('fs.read_file', ({ context }) => ({ path: context.path })),
        on: {
          TOOL_RESULT: { target: 'done', actions: assign({ result: ({ event }) => event.result }) },
          TOOL_ERROR: 'failed',
        },
      },
      done: { type: 'final' },
      failed: { type: 'final' },
    },
    output: ({ context }) => ({ result: context.result }),
  });

Example — handling a denied approval (run with input: { path }):

  import { setup, assign } from 'xstate';
  import { toolCall } from '@astral-mcp/tools';

  export default setup({}).createMachine({
    id: 'writeOne',
    context: ({ input }) => ({ path: input.path, status: 'pending' }),
    initial: 'writing',
    states: {
      writing: {
        entry: toolCall('fs.write_file', ({ context }) => ({ path: context.path, content: 'hello' })),
        on: {
          TOOL_RESULT: { target: 'done', actions: assign({ status: 'written' }) },
          TOOL_DENIED: { target: 'done', actions: assign({ status: 'skipped' }) },
          TOOL_ERROR: { target: 'done', actions: assign({ status: 'failed' }) },
        },
      },
      done: { type: 'final' },
    },
    output: ({ context }) => ({ status: context.status }),
  });

Tools 1–14 of 14 (in the fs box):
- fs.read_file — Read the complete contents of a file as text. [runs immediately]
- fs.read_text_file — Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. [runs immediately]
- fs.read_media_file — Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. [runs immediately]
- fs.read_multiple_files — Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. [runs immediately]
- fs.write_file — Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. [asks for approval, destructive]
- fs.edit_file — Make line-based edits to a text file. [asks for approval, destructive]
- fs.create_directory — Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. [asks for approval]
- fs.list_directory — Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. [runs immediately]
- fs.list_directory_with_sizes — Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes. [runs immediately]
- fs.directory_tree — Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. [runs immediately]
- fs.move_file — Move or rename files and directories. [asks for approval, destructive]
- fs.search_files — Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. [runs immediately]
- fs.get_file_info — Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. [runs immediately]
- fs.list_allowed_directories — Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. [runs immediately]
